The Sons Of The Forest is super entertaining. The game has lots of interesting mechanics, the building is intuitive as well as fun. Combat feels good, and the exploration is rewarding. Fun items, and loot crafting system is awesome. Highly recommended, this game is a great underrated, although extremely entertaining addition. Plus for $30 it is a steal.

A game where you must survive cannibals... How ironic when you turn around, proceed to bash their skull in then become the cannibal yourself. The only game where it's okay to kill humans and eat them, 100/10 highly recommend.

Jokes aside this game takes the survival / horror experience to another level, the insane building mechanics combined with the jaw dropping environments from the terrifying caves to the lush and dense forests. It all comes together to make a survival experience unlike other games can do. This game is also better with friends!

Keep in mind this game is early access (as of this review) I have personally experienced some bugs,

EX: Not being able to place down stick paths
EX: Not being able to interact
EX: Arms glitched when drinking and opening inventory

These are pretty harmless and fix when restarting the game but still pretty annoying, as a fan of the series I can ignore these very little issues and I am sure they will get fixed in the future.

If your looking for a fun survival / horror game this is your game to get!

The game itself is gorgeous: graphics, building and combat mechanics, interacting with enemies and realistic friendly fire are a treat. It's an enjoyable game if you're into exploring for days, building a base, getting spooked in caves and finding out there's always an enemy spookier than the first one you've met.

But after playing The Forest (1) and looking forward to getting another forest game, the story was really disappointing. I've spent days playing, exploring, reading notes and fighting all enemies throughout the forest and across the island and never had any clue about any storyline or whatsoever. Suddenly, I came to the point of the story ending, without knowing what it actually was about.
It just doesn't add up to each other, from golfballs to cubes.
I get the whole fresh storyline and different take on the game, but I wasn't invested in the story as I was when playing The Forest. Clues don't add up and just add more confusing information, which adds up to more confusing information.

TLDR: Sweet game for fun foresting/exploring/hunting nights with the homies, not so great storyline. Would still recommend.

I would recommend this game BUT with a caveat! Don't buy it right now if you want to play it immediately for the whole experience.

The game is incomplete and TBH quite barren. Honestly i would wait a few MONTHS at least (winter 2023 even) Because by then they should have more of a filled out game.

Honestly, the "infinite enemies" thing just ruins the whole game for me. I could kill a trillion cannibals, and there'd be another party of them coming along in 5 minutes. Same complaint about the first game, but I slogged through it. Bases brimming with traps, just to keep the cannibals from kidnapping you 3 times a day.

Other problems? The inventory interface is hot garbage; slow and clunky. Many actions lock you into an animation, while the rest of the game keeps on going (i.e. killing you)

Is there actually a story here? There's a lot here that *could* be good, garbage UI aside. But the Turbo Spawning Bottomless Hordes ruined it all for me. I even whipped out godmode and realized I don't care about this game. Ugh, I'm done, uninstalled.

Do not buy.

This game isn’t as good as The Forest.

In The Forest, you had limited resources, tools, and weapons.

In Sons of the Forest, food respawns in containers upon reloading a save, removing the need to hunt animals for sustenance. Additionally, tools like the smartphone or GPS diminish the sense of wonder and exploration. Lastly, guns make combat feel trivial by reducing the danger of mutants.

I changed two settings and found the game to be more enjoyable. I turned the enemy scout parties to low and the enemy health to low. I had to watch a few guides on youtube to get started on what to do because there isn't much guidance or prompts (but that makes it fun in it's own way). If you like Subnautica, this game is right up your alley. I've enjoyed it and find myself thinking of my next play session when offline.

The game is incredibly lame.

Their sound queues are completely broken, when they scurry next to you,
they sound like they're 50 meters away.
The building system is completely different, and more difficult to get into.
Animals and cannibals are constantly clipping through rocks and map geometry.
Movement is still floaty.
Honestly the whole experience feels like a unity game, a slightly visually improved original,
but worse in every other aspect apart from graphics.
Do not recommend.
